title: The five-speed lonely runner spectrum below 1/5: a kernel-checked proof
description: A complete formalization in Lean 4 with Mathlib of the statement that for five distinct positive integer speeds the values of the maximum loneliness ML below 1/5 are exactly s/(5s+1) with s >= 1 (the inclusion, the attainment of every value by (1,2,3,4,5s), and the equivalence), with no hypothesis left over and with no sorry, no native_decide, and no axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The proof is a computer-assisted case analysis whose finite certificate (1,965 representatives of second-level nodes, 81,436 leaf classes, 9,593,060 lines, as counted in the paper) is produced by Rust programs and checked by the Lean kernel, together with an exact analysis of two infinite families on the critical tori. The method is that of Yi, Gill and Bu for four speeds (arXiv:2610.40694); no first proof is claimed, and whether another complete proof of the five-speed statement exists must be checked against the literature (the last prior-art searches were made on 15 and 17 November 2026). The archive contains the paper (17 pages), 9,312 Lean modules of a 17,598-module import closure (the other 8,286 generated modules, 669.5 MB, are listed with sha256 and restored by a script), the Rust generators and a reproduction entry point; a from-scratch build is about 36.8 hours of Lean time (a cost-model figure; no clean rebuild was run). The Lean modules, the Rust generators and the first draft of the paper were produced by an AI system (Claude, Anthropic); fresh sessions of the same system reviewed them; the questions, the research directions and the decision to formalize this statement came from Vico Bonfioli. The Lean kernel, not a human reader, checks the proofs. The paper has not been peer reviewed. No proof of the lonely runner conjecture is claimed. Comments in some Lean modules and generator sources were edited for the public release; Lean declarations and proofs are unchanged, and the checksums in the archive are those of the shipped files.
